# Financial Logic

This document defines every number the application shows. Formulas are implemented in
`src/finance/calculations.py` (pure functions), `src/finance/forecasting.py` and `src/finance/budget_analysis.py`.
**No figure is generated by AI.**

> All figures in the sample dataset are **illustrative** and are not Hummingbirds financial information.

---

## 1. Conventions

| Convention | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Base (reporting) currency** | EUR (`config/settings.yaml → base_currency`) |
| **Currency conversion** | `amount_base = amount / rate[currency]`, where `rate` = units of currency per 1 EUR (`fx_rates` in config). Conversion happens **before** any aggregation. Amounts in different currencies are never added directly. |
| **Missing FX rate** | `amount_base` = NaN and the row is excluded from totals **with a visible warning**. It is never treated as zero or as EUR. Upload validation rejects such rows. |
| **Variance sign** | **Variance = Actual (or Forecast) − Budget.** **Positive = overspend**, **negative = underspend**. |
| **Periods** | Months as `YYYY-MM`. "To date" = all budget months up to and including the selected *as-of* month. |
| **Budget phase** | The months that have approved budget lines. Sample: April 2026 – March 2027 (FY2026/27). |
| **Credit notes** | Negative transaction amounts. They reduce actual expenditure and are flagged. |
| **Division by zero / missing data** | Ratios return NaN, shown as "n/a", never 0%. |
| **Rounding** | Amounts are stored at full precision, rounded to cents in calculations and to whole euros on screen. |

## 2. Core measures

| Measure | Formula | Function |
|---|---|---|
| Total approved budget | Σ `budgets.amount_base` (all months in the phase) | `calculations.total_approved_budget` |
| Budget phased to date | Σ `budgets.amount_base` for months ≤ as-of | `total_approved_budget(budgets, periods)` |
| Actual expenditure to date | Σ `transactions.amount_base` for months ≤ as-of within the phase | `calculations.total_actual_expenditure` |
| Remaining approved budget | Approved budget − Actual to date | `calculations.remaining_budget` |
| Actual variance (vs full budget) | Actual − Approved budget | `calculations.budget_variance` |
| Variance to date | Actual to date − Budget phased to date | `budget_variance(actual, budget_to_date)` |
| Variance % | Variance ÷ the budget it is measured against × 100 | `calculations.variance_percentage` |
| Budget utilisation % | Actual to date ÷ Approved budget × 100 | `calculations.budget_utilisation` |
| Category-wise expenditure | Σ `amount_base` grouped by category | `calculations.category_expenditure` |
| Monthly expenditure | Σ `amount_base` grouped by `YYYY-MM` | `calculations.monthly_expenditure` |
| Monthly budget vs actual (window) | Phased budget and actual per month; variance = actual − budget; a category filter applies to both | `budget_analysis.monthly_budget_vs_actual` |

**Why two variances?** Part-way through the year, actual − *full* budget is always negative and says little about
performance. The **variance to date** (against the budget phased to the same months) is the meaningful in-year
measure. Both are shown, and both follow the same sign convention.

## 3. Forecasting

```
Forecast remaining (category c, month m > as-of)
    = forecasts.forecast_amount(c, m)        if the analyst entered a forecast
    = budgets.approved_amount(c, m)          otherwise ("budget-as-forecast" fallback, labelled in the detail table)

Adjusted remaining = Forecast remaining × (1 + scenario% / 100) × (1 + category% / 100)

Forecast at Completion (FAC)        = Actual Expenditure to Date + Forecast Remaining Expenditure
Forecast Budget Variance            = FAC − Approved Budget
Forecast Variance %                 = Forecast Budget Variance / Approved Budget × 100
```

Rules:
- **Actual spend is never adjusted** by a scenario. Scenarios only change money not yet spent.
- Forecasts for months that already have actuals (≤ as-of) are ignored. **Actuals take precedence.**
- Scenarios (`config/settings.yaml → scenarios`): Base 0%, Optimistic −7.5%, Pessimistic +12.5% on remaining spend.
  The analyst can change these on the Forecasting page.
- **Run-rate cross-check** (shown for comparison only): average monthly spend of the last 3 closed months × remaining
  months. It ignores seasonality, so it is not the official forecast.
- No machine learning is used. Every forecast figure traces to a row in the detail table and its written assumption.

### Worked example (test case in `tests/test_calculations.py`)

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Approved budget | €2,000,000 |
| Actual expenditure to date | €900,000 |
| Forecast remaining expenditure | €1,300,000 |
| **Forecast at completion** | €900,000 + €1,300,000 = **€2,200,000** |
| **Forecast budget variance** | €2,200,000 − €2,000,000 = **+€200,000 (overspend)** |
| Forecast variance % | 200,000 / 2,000,000 × 100 = **+10.0%** |
| Remaining approved budget | €2,000,000 − €900,000 = €1,100,000 |
| Budget utilisation | 900,000 / 2,000,000 = 45.0% |
| Status | **Potential Overspend** (10% > 5% threshold) |

## 4. Financial status rules

Evaluated in `budget_analysis.determine_financial_status`. Thresholds are in `config/settings.yaml → status_rules`.
Potential Overspend rules are checked first, then Watchlist rules. The page shows every rule and whether it fired.

| Status | Rule (any one triggers) | Default threshold |
|---|---|---|
| **Potential Overspend** | Forecast variance % > threshold | 5.0% |
| | Actual to date already exceeds the full approved budget | — |
| **Watchlist** | Forecast variance % > threshold | 0.0% |
| | Any category's forecast variance % > threshold | 10.0% |
| | Variance to date % (vs phased budget) > threshold | 5.0% |
| | Spend recorded against an unbudgeted or unrecognised category | — |
| **Within Budget** | No rule triggered | — |

There is no composite or AI "health score". The status is a deterministic consequence of the rules above.

## 5. Transaction flags

Implemented in `budget_analysis.transaction_flags`.

| Flag | Rule |
|---|---|
| Duplicate transaction ID | The ID occurs more than once (all occurrences flagged) |
| Duplicate invoice reference | The non-blank invoice ID occurs more than once, which may mean a double payment |
| Missing values | supplier, description, invoice_id or document_reference is blank |
| Uncategorised | Category is not one of the recognised categories (includes "Uncategorised") |
| Category budget exceeded | The running total of the category (by date) exceeds its full approved budget |
| Unusually large | amount_base > 4 × category median **and** ≥ €5,000 (`anomaly_rules`) |
| Credit note | amount < 0 |
| No FX rate | Currency has no configured rate |
| Outside budget phase | Month not in the budget phase |

## 6. Monthly report rules

- **Significant deviation:** |variance %| > 10% **and** |variance| > €10,000 (`reporting` in config). Tested on both
  the to-date and at-completion bases, for budgeted categories only.
- **Observations** restate calculated figures (largest over- and underspend, month vs budget, FAC). They never state a
  cause, because the records contain none. Explanations come only from the human-written **analyst commentary**.
- **Items requiring management attention:** the status (if not Within Budget), overspend deviations, duplicate
  invoices, uncategorised and queried items, unusually large items, pending-verification totals and failed
  reconciliations.

## 7. Reconciliation checks

`budget_analysis.reconciliation_checks` runs on every page load (Overview expander, report sheet). Tolerance is €0.01.

1. Σ category budgets = total approved budget
2. Σ monthly budgets = total approved budget
3. Σ category actuals = transaction register total (to date)
4. Σ monthly actuals = transaction register total (to date)
5. FAC = actual to date + forecast remaining

The tests assert that all five pass for **every** as-of month of the sample dataset.

## 8. The illustrative sample dataset

Generated by `src/data/sample_data.py` (deterministic seed, so it is reproducible).

| Element | Value / assumption |
|---|---|
| Budget phase | FY2026/27, April 2026 – March 2027 (12 months) |
| Approved budget | **€2,400,000** across 11 categories, phased monthly with seasonal weights (seedlings and land preparation early, planting through the rains, monitoring later). The last month absorbs rounding, so totals reconcile exactly. |
| Actuals | April – October 2026: **234 transactions**, 15 fictional suppliers, 174 in UGX and 60 in EUR (UGX converted at 4,100/EUR) |
| Behaviour built in | Transport +22% (fuel), personnel +6%, monitoring −28%, community −15% vs phased budget; one unplanned €24,500 equipment replacement |
| Forecasts | November 2026 – March 2027 per category, each with a written assumption (e.g. "Fuel cost ~15% above budget assumption expected to persist") |
| Resulting position (as at Oct 2026) | Actual €1.56m (64.9% used, +2.8% vs phased budget). FAC €2.46m (+€61.7k, **+2.6%**). Status **Watchlist**. |

**Planted data-quality issues** (so the register and report have real cases to show):

| Transaction | Issue |
|---|---|
| TXN-2026-0191 / TXN-2026-0232 | Same supplier, invoice INV-2331 and amount booked twice (possible double payment) |
| TXN-2026-0233 | Category left blank by the accountant, so stored as "Uncategorised" |
| TXN-2026-0234 | Credit note (−UGX 9.84m) for seedlings rejected on delivery |
| TXN-2026-0044, TXN-2026-0121 | Missing supporting document reference |
| TXN-2026-0150 | Unplanned emergency equipment replacement (€24,500), flagged as unusually large |
| 3 random transactions | Status "Queried" |

The upload test file `upload_example_transactions_with_errors.csv` contains 17 rows. Each one demonstrates a
validation rule, and the `test_note` column names it.

## 9. Assumptions and limitations of the financial logic

- FX uses fixed illustrative planning rates, not transaction-date rates. FX gains and losses are not modelled.
- Transactions are treated as expenditure when recorded (accruals basis). There is no separate cash or commitments
  ledger.
- All transaction statuses count towards actuals. Pending and queried amounts are disclosed separately, so the
  analyst can judge how firm the figures are.
- The budget phase is the only "completion" horizon. Multi-year lifecycle costs are out of scope for v0.1.
